# Render the skills for every agent from one source

## Intent

`af-prd`, `af-spec` and `af-impl` put `spec`, `specr` and `speca` to work in
a person's own session, but they reach one agent and load more text than a
step needs. They are Claude Code files, installed into Claude Code's
directory, and their text uses Claude Code's argument placeholder and slash
syntax. `af-spec` is 40 KB and `af-impl` 35 KB, all of it in context for
every step of a run. Codex, Cursor and GitHub Copilot load skills in the same
directory layout, so the method can reach them from one source with a render
per agent. Each skill becomes a body that carries the order of the run, its
gates and its refusals, plus reference files the agent reads at the step they
serve. One source tree renders and installs the three skills for each agent,
and refuses a skill whose body would load more than 24 KB at once. What the
skills do does not change; where it is written does.

## Goals

- `make install-skills AGENT=<agent>` installs the three skills for `claude`,
  `codex`, `cursor` or `copilot`, each into that agent's user skill
  directory. `make install-skills` with no `AGENT` does what it does today:
  installs for Claude Code into `~/.claude/skills`.
- An installed skill works in its agent with no edit. Its frontmatter carries
  only the keys that agent reads. Every invocation of another skill in its
  text is written in that agent's syntax. Every reference file it links is in
  its own directory.
- The `SKILL.md` body of every rendered skill, for every agent, is at most
  24,576 bytes.
- `make check` fails on a skill that breaks a render rule, and names the
  file and the rule. The rules: a body over the limit, a link to a reference
  file that does not exist, a name that does not match its directory, an
  invocation of a skill that does not exist.
- A run of each skill follows the same steps, takes the same gates and stops
  for the same reasons as before the change. The one new action is reading a
  named reference file at the step it serves.
- `af-spec`, when it writes the PRD itself, writes it to the same shape as
  `af-prd`, read from the same file, without `af-prd` being loaded.
- `make install-skills AGENT=<agent> PROJECT=<path>` installs into that
  repository's project skill directory, so a team can commit the skills for
  an agent that reads only repository skills, such as Copilot's cloud agent.

## Non-goals

- Running `spec` on another vendor's model. The generator stays Claude-only,
  as `docs/spec-kit-comparison.md` §7.1 says.
- Changing what any skill does: its method, its gates, its refusals, the
  commands it calls, its report. A change the split shows to be needed is a
  change of its own.
- Agents other than these four, Gemini CLI among them. Adding one is a row in
  the agent table and a later change.
- Command and prompt files: Cursor commands, Copilot prompt files, Codex
  custom prompts. All four agents load skills directly, and a wrapper would
  be a second copy to keep in step.
- Installing without a checkout: a release archive per agent, a plugin or
  marketplace entry, the skills embedded in `speca`. These belong with
  tagging a release (§7.1 item 6 of the comparison).
- Committing the rendered skills to the repository.
- A template language. The render substitutes one token, filters the
  frontmatter and copies the linked files; no other text is rewritten.
- Measuring whether the smaller skills produce better packages or better
  code (§7.3 of the comparison). This change shows that they behave the same.
- The `af-impl` block quoted in `docs/specr.md` and `docs/speca.md`. It is an
  example of a skill's step, not a copy of `af-impl`, and stays as it is.
- `docs/spec-kit-comparison.md` itself, which is an analysis dated
  2026-10-28 and stays as written.
- Install paths on Windows, which are best effort as the steering file says.

## Background

`skills/` holds three files with no extension: `af-prd` (17,504 bytes, 330
lines), `af-spec` (40,317 bytes, 746 lines) and `af-impl` (34,702 bytes, 594
lines). Each opens with frontmatter carrying `name`, `description` and
`argument-hint`. `make install-skills` copies each one to
`~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, and `make uninstall-skills` removes
`~/.claude/skills/<name>` for each name. No other directory and no other
agent is served. `make clean` removes `build/` and `coverage.txt`.

The text the skills hold for Claude Code alone is small:

- `$ARGUMENTS`, five times: three in `af-impl`, one in `af-prd`, one in
  `af-spec`;
- three slash invocations of another skill: `/af-prd` in `af-spec` §1, and
  `/af-impl` in the next steps of `af-spec` §12 and `af-prd` §8;
- the `argument-hint` key in each frontmatter.

The rest is already neutral. The skills name `AGENTS.md` beside `CLAUDE.md`
and say "if you have a task-list tool".

The comparison recommends moving "the JSON shapes, the field tables" into
files read on demand so that each body fits under 24 KB. Measured, that is
not enough. In `af-spec` the code blocks and tables are 7.3 KB, and moving
them alone leaves about 33 KB. In `af-impl` they are 0.5 KB. Its bulk is
procedure for one phase at a time:

- reading `speca`'s and `specr`'s output (§1);
- writing tests first (§5, step 4);
- the conformance pass (§6);
- the pull request and the issues for its open items (§7).

The split therefore goes by phase.

Several things are written more than once across the skills:

- how to read `speca`'s and `specr`'s JSON;
- their exit codes;
- sending `--markdown-file` and stdout to files outside the repository;
- what to do when the commands are not installed;
- the `make build` line;
- the vague words the validator flags;
- the size limits of one package.

`af-spec` §1 tells the agent, when no PRD exists and the person chooses this
run to write one, to write it "to `af-prd`'s shape". That shape is defined
only in `af-prd` §4. Installed or loaded alone, `af-spec` carries no
definition of it.

The other three agents read the same layout, a directory per skill holding a
`SKILL.md`, from their own directories, and two of them also read Claude
Code's:

- **Cursor** reads `.cursor/skills/` and `~/.cursor/skills/`. For
  compatibility it also reads `.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/` and
  `.codex/skills/`.
- **Copilot** reads `.github/skills/`, `.claude/skills/` and
  `.agents/skills/` in a repository, and `~/.copilot/skills/`,
  `~/.claude/skills/` and `~/.agents/skills/` for a user.
- **Codex** reads `$CODEX_HOME/skills/`, by default `~/.codex/skills/`, and a
  skill is invoked as `$name`.

None of this could be read at its source from where this PRD was written
(see *Verified External API*). One consequence holds whatever the final
paths are: a Claude Code install in `~/.claude/skills` already reaches
Copilot, and installing for Copilot as well loads each skill twice there.

The 24 KB figure is the cap EGM's harnesses put on a skill body (§4.11 of the
comparison). Claude Code's own guidance is to keep `SKILL.md` under 500 lines
and to move detailed reference material into separate files.

## Requirements

### The source

- Each skill is a directory `skills/<name>/` holding `SKILL.md`, which is the
  frontmatter and the body. Its own reference files are in
  `skills/<name>/references/`. Reference files linked by more than one skill
  are in `skills/_shared/references/`. A directory under `skills/` whose name
  starts with `_` is not a skill.
- A skill links a reference file with a Markdown link whose target is
  `references/<file>.md`. The link is the inclusion. A file is rendered into
  a skill when that skill's `SKILL.md` links it, or when a reference file
  already included links it. A link resolves in the skill's own
  `references/` first, then in `skills/_shared/references/`.
- `{{invoke <name>}}`, in a body or a reference file, stands for an
  invocation of the skill `<name>`. It is the only token the render replaces.
- The skill text names its argument in words ("the argument the skill was
  given"), not with a placeholder.

### Rendering

- `make skills` renders every skill for every agent into
  `build/skills/<agent>/<name>/`: its `SKILL.md`, and a `references/`
  directory holding each file the skill links, directly or through another
  reference file. A file nothing links is not rendered. `make clean` removes
  the output with the rest of `build/`.
- Rendering makes no model call and no network call, and needs no
  credential. It does not run `update-agentkit`.
- For each agent, the frontmatter keeps only the keys in this table, in the
  source's order. The body and the reference files are unchanged except for
  the token.

  | Agent | Frontmatter keys kept | `{{invoke af-impl}}` becomes |
  |---|---|---|
  | `claude` | `name`, `description`, `argument-hint`, `disable-model-invocation` | `/af-impl` |
  | `codex` | `name`, `description` | `$af-impl` |
  | `cursor` | `name`, `description`, `disable-model-invocation` | `/af-impl` |
  | `copilot` | `name`, `description` | `/af-impl` |

- The same source renders to byte-identical output on every run.
- A render replaces the previous output of `make skills` whole, so a file
  removed from the source is not left in `build/skills/`.

### What the render refuses

The render reports every problem it finds in one run, not the first only.
Each problem is one line on stderr, `<source path>: <problem>`. On any
problem it exits non-zero and writes nothing, for any agent. These are the
problems:

- a skill directory with no `SKILL.md`, or a `SKILL.md` with no frontmatter
  or with frontmatter that is not YAML;
- a `name` that is missing, that differs from the directory name, or that
  breaks the Agent Skills rule: 1 to 64 characters, lowercase letters,
  digits and single hyphens, neither first nor last character a hyphen;
- a `description` that is missing, empty, or longer than 1,024 characters;
- a link to `references/<file>.md` that resolves in neither directory, for
  example
  `skills/af-spec/SKILL.md: links references/tasks.md, which is in neither skills/af-spec/references/ nor skills/_shared/references/`;
- a reference file name present in both the skill's own `references/` and
  `skills/_shared/references/`;
- `{{invoke <name>}}` naming no skill under `skills/`, and any other `{{…}}`
  token;
- a rendered body longer than 24,576 bytes for any agent, measured in bytes
  of UTF-8 after the line that closes the frontmatter and after the token is
  replaced, for example
  `skills/af-spec/SKILL.md: body is 31,204 bytes for codex, 6,628 over the 24,576-byte limit`.
  A body of exactly 24,576 bytes passes. Reference files have no limit.

Two findings are warnings, which go to stderr and leave the exit code 0:

- a file in a skill's own `references/` that nothing links:
  `skills/af-impl/references/old.md: linked by nothing; not rendered`;
- a file in `skills/_shared/references/` that no skill links.

### Installing and uninstalling

- `make install-skills [AGENT=<agent>] [PROJECT=<path>] [SKILLS_DIR=<dir>]`
  renders the skills for the agent and copies each one to `<dir>/<name>/`.
  `AGENT` defaults to `claude`. The directory is the agent's user directory,
  or its project directory under `PROJECT` when `PROJECT` is given.
  `SKILLS_DIR` overrides both.

  | Agent | User directory | Project directory |
  |---|---|---|
  | `claude` | `~/.claude/skills` | `<PROJECT>/.claude/skills` |
  | `codex` | `$CODEX_HOME/skills`, else `~/.codex/skills` | `<PROJECT>/.agents/skills` |
  | `cursor` | `~/.cursor/skills` | `<PROJECT>/.cursor/skills` |
  | `copilot` | `~/.copilot/skills` | `<PROJECT>/.github/skills` |

- It prints `installed: <name> -> <dir>/<name>` for each skill, and exits 0.
- It replaces `<dir>/<name>/` whole, so a reference file removed from the
  source is not left installed. It changes no other directory under `<dir>`.
- On a render problem it installs nothing, prints the problems as `make
  skills` does, and exits non-zero.
- An `AGENT` outside the four exits non-zero with
  `unknown agent "<value>"; one of: claude, codex, cursor, copilot`, and
  writes nothing.
- A `PROJECT` that is not an existing directory exits non-zero with
  `PROJECT <path> is not a directory`, and writes nothing.
- When the agent also reads a directory of another agent (see the table in
  *Background*) and that directory already holds a skill of the same name,
  the install prints
  `warning: <agent> also loads <path>/<name>; it will see <name> twice` and
  installs all the same.
- `make uninstall-skills [AGENT] [PROJECT] [SKILLS_DIR]` resolves the same
  directory and removes `<dir>/<name>` for each of the three skill names,
  printing `removed: <name>`. A name that is not installed is skipped without
  a message. Nothing else under `<dir>` is touched.

### Agent-neutral text

- No rendered skill, for any agent, contains `$ARGUMENTS`, and none names
  another skill in another agent's invocation syntax.
- In Claude Code the argument still reaches the skill. When no placeholder
  is present, Claude Code appends `ARGUMENTS: <input>` to the skill's
  content.
- `af-impl` carries `disable-model-invocation: true`. In Claude Code and
  Cursor it then runs only when the person invokes it. `af-prd` and
  `af-spec` stay invocable by the model.

### The skills' content

- Each body keeps:
  - the paragraph of rules that opens it;
  - the run's order and its list of reasons to stop;
  - every numbered step, with the commands that gate it;
  - *Never*;
  - the report.

  A rule that stops the run, a gate or an item of *Never* is never only in a
  reference file.
- Each step whose detail moved opens with an instruction to read the file
  before acting: "Read [references/<file>.md](references/<file>.md) in full
  before …".
- The detail moves to these files:

  | File | Holds | Linked by |
  |---|---|---|
  | `_shared/references/prd-shape.md` | the PRD's sections in order and what each holds (`af-prd` §4); the vague words and the size of one package (`af-prd` §6) | `af-prd` §4 and §6; `af-spec` §1 and §5 |
  | `_shared/references/speca-specr.md` | the result fields of `speca` and `specr`, their exit codes 0, 1 and 2, writing `--markdown-file` and stdout to files outside the repository, the install line, what to do when the commands are not installed | all three |
  | `af-spec/references/prd-frontmatter.md` | §5: the frontmatter and its field table, the three scaffolds, the encoding | `af-spec` §5 |
  | `af-spec/references/requirements.md` | §6: the example, the ids, the EARS patterns, contracts, the glossary, execution paths, `external_apis` | `af-spec` §6 |
  | `af-spec/references/test-spec.md` | §7: the example, the fields and kinds, the coverage rules, one test per behaviour | `af-spec` §7 |
  | `af-spec/references/tasks.md` | §8: the example, the fields, `test_commands`, `dependencies`, the plan's rules, the integration task | `af-spec` §8 |
  | `af-spec/references/architecture.md` | §9: when to write it and its sections | `af-spec` §9 |
  | `af-spec/references/verdict.md` | §10: the stages of the verdict and their order, the warnings worth acting on, validating without `speca` | `af-spec` §10 |
  | `af-impl/references/test-first.md` | §5, step 4, and the integration task | `af-impl` §5 |
  | `af-impl/references/conformance.md` | §6: the checklist and the `unmet` list | `af-impl` §6 |
  | `af-impl/references/landing.md` | §7: the pull request body, tracking the open items with `issue`, the fallbacks | `af-impl` §7 |

- Nothing is lost. Every instruction of the three current skills is, after
  the change, in a body or a reference file, or it is in a list of deliberate
  cuts, each with its reason, in the description of the pull request that
  makes the change. Text written more than once and collapsed into one shared
  file counts as kept.

### Showing that the skills behave the same

- Before the change merges, each skill is run once in Claude Code and once
  in Codex, in a scratch repository, before the change and after it, on the
  same input:
  - `af-prd` on an idea of two sentences;
  - `af-spec` on a PRD of one or two requirement areas;
  - `af-impl` on a package of two tasks.
- Each run after the change:
  - reads each linked reference file at the step that links it;
  - takes the same gates;
  - ends at the same stop, or the same end;
  - for `af-spec`, ends with a package that `speca --validate` reports
    `valid`.
- What each pair of runs showed, and any difference, is written in the pull
  request.

### Documentation and build

- `make check` runs the render's checks after `test`, with no network and no
  API key.
- `make help` lists `skills`, `skills-check`, `install-skills` and
  `uninstall-skills`.
- `README.md`, *Agent Skills*: the four agents, the install line for each,
  and the note that a Claude Code install already reaches Copilot. Its table
  of make targets gains the new ones.
- `docs/configuration.md`: `AGENT`, `PROJECT` and `SKILLS_DIR`.
- `docs/architecture.md`: the source layout, the render and the install.
- An ADR records the decision and the two agent tables. For each row it
  gives the date the row was confirmed against that vendor's documentation.
- `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md`, *Repository Layout*: a line for `skills/`, and
  one for wherever the render lives.

## Design Decisions

1. **One source in the Agent Skills layout, and no format per agent.** All
   four agents load `SKILL.md` directories. Command or prompt files would be
   a second copy of each skill.
2. **The split goes by phase, not by data shape.** The shapes and tables are
   7.3 KB of `af-spec` and 0.5 KB of `af-impl`. Moving only them leaves both
   over the limit.
3. **The link is the inclusion.** A manifest of the files each skill uses
   would be one more thing to keep in step. With the link as the record, a
   broken link is found by the same check.
4. **One name in both directories is an error, not an override.** A skill's
   own file shadowing a shared one would let one skill drift from its
   siblings without a word.
5. **One token, no template language.** The invocation of another skill is
   the only text that differs by agent. The argument is named in words,
   which every agent reads the same.
6. **The 24,576-byte ceiling is on the body only, per agent.** The body is
   loaded with the skill, and the reference files only at their step. The
   ceiling is measured in bytes, not lines, because bytes are what load.
7. **The ceiling is a check in `make check`, not a Go test of the skills.**
   The steering file forbids tests of a document's content. The render's own
   behaviour is what the tests cover.
8. **The rendered skills are not committed.** Users of the other agents
   still need `speca` and `specr`, which need Go and a checkout until a
   release exists. Archives per agent come with the release.
9. **No new command.** The render runs through `make`, and the public
   surface of the repository does not grow (§4.2 of the comparison).
10. **`AGENT` defaults to `claude`**, so `make install-skills` does what it
    did.
11. **An install replaces a skill's directory whole, and an uninstall
    touches only the three names**, so neither leaves stale files nor
    removes a skill it did not install.
12. **A skill found twice is a warning, not a refusal.** The person may use
    both agents on one machine.
13. **`af-prd` and `af-spec` stay invocable by the model.** They write files
    in the working tree and nothing beyond it.
14. **Provisional: `af-impl` runs only when invoked**
    (`disable-model-invocation: true`) in Claude Code and Cursor. It pushes
    branches and opens pull requests and issues, which a person should start.
    It is provisional because it changes how `af-impl` starts today in
    Claude Code. Codex and Copilot have no verified equivalent, so there it
    stays invocable by the model. Codex's `agents/openai.yaml` may carry one,
    which the ADR settles.
15. **Provisional: the agent directories are the ones in the install
    table.** They come from secondary sources and could not be read at their
    vendor's documentation (see below). `SKILLS_DIR` overrides any of them,
    and the ADR records each row as confirmed, with its date, before the
    change merges.

16. **The render lives in `internal/skillgen`, as a `package main` that `make`
    runs with `go run ./internal/skillgen`.** The PRD forbids a new command,
    and `cmd/` is where `make build` installs commands from. `internal/` is
    excluded from `make doc`, so the render adds nothing to the public
    surface, and the repository already tests a `package main` with its tests
    beside it (`cmd/speca`). It imports only the standard library and
    `github.com/goccy/go-yaml`, which `go.mod` already carries, so no make
    target of the render depends on `update-agentkit` and none reaches the
    network.
17. **The same program renders, installs and uninstalls**, under `--check`,
    `--install` and `--uninstall`, and the `make` targets only pass `AGENT`,
    `PROJECT` and `SKILLS_DIR` through to it. Resolving the agent
    directories, replacing a skill's directory whole and warning about a
    skill loaded twice are behaviours with their own tests; in shell they
    would have none.
18. **The frontmatter is filtered line by line on its top-level keys**, each
    kept key keeping its own text and its continuation lines. It is parsed
    with `go-yaml` only to read and check `name` and `description`.
    Re-marshalling a parsed map would lose the source's key order, which the
    render is required to keep.
19. **`$ARGUMENTS`, and a skill named in an agent's own invocation syntax,
    are render refusals.** The PRD requires that no rendered skill carry
    either and that `make check` fail on a skill that breaks a render rule,
    but its list of refusals has no check for it; without one the
    requirement is enforced by nobody. A name is matched only where it
    stands alone — `/af-impl` or `$af-impl` preceded by the start of a line,
    whitespace or an opening delimiter and followed by the end of a line,
    whitespace or punctuation — so that the path `skills/af-impl` in prose is
    not a refusal.
20. **The editorial guarantees are task steps, not acceptance criteria.**
    Which sections each body keeps, that nothing is lost, and the before and
    after runs in two agents are work a reviewer confirms, not an outcome a
    program can observe, and Decision 7 keeps the skills' text out of the Go
    tests. They are steps and `done_when` entries of the tasks that carry
    them. What a program can observe — that the committed `skills/` tree
    renders for all four agents with no problem — is a criterion.
21. **The documentation obligations are task steps too.** `README.md`,
    `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, the ADR and the
    *Repository Layout* line are required by the steering file in the same
    session, and it forbids tests of a document's content, so they are steps
    of the tasks that change the behaviour they describe.

## Dependencies

- **ADR 05** (`specr`) and **ADR 10** (`speca`): the skills call both
  commands as they are, and nothing in them changes.
- **`docs/spec-kit-comparison.md`** §4.11 and §7.1, item 3: the
  recommendation this PRD carries out, corrected where *Background* says.
- No package under `.specs/` is changed or depended on.
- The skill loaders of Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and GitHub Copilot, below.

## Verified External API

- **`github.com/goccy/go-yaml` v1.19.2**, in `go.mod`, parses the PRD
  frontmatter in `afspec/prd.go`. `func Unmarshal(data []byte, v
  interface{}) error`, read with `go doc`.
- **`io/fs`** and **`testing/fstest`**, the standard library:
  `type MapFS map[string]*MapFile`, read with `go doc`.
- **Claude Code skills**, read at <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills>
  on 2026-11-06:
  - when no placeholder in the content receives the arguments, "Claude Code
    appends `ARGUMENTS: <your input>` to the end of the skill content";
  - the frontmatter keys include `name`, `description`, `argument-hint`,
    `disable-model-invocation`, `metadata`, `license` and `compatibility`,
    all optional;
  - "Claude Code ignores a field it doesn't recognize without reporting an
    error";
  - `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` is the directory holding the skill's `SKILL.md`;
  - the personal location is `~/.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md`, the
    project location `.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md`;
  - "Keep `SKILL.md` under 500 lines. Move detailed reference material to
    separate files."
- **Agent Skills specification** (<https://agentskills.io/specification>):
  **unverified**. The host was not reachable from where this PRD was
  written. Assumed: `name` is 1 to 64 lowercase letters, digits and single
  hyphens, matches its directory, and does not start or end with a hyphen;
  `description` is at most 1,024 characters; `references/` beside
  `SKILL.md` holds files read on demand, resolved from the skill's
  directory.
- **Codex skills** (<https://developers.openai.com/codex/skills>):
  **unverified**, host not reachable. Assumed from third-party copies of the
  page:
  - user skills in `$CODEX_HOME/skills/`, by default `~/.codex/skills/`, and
    admin skills in `/etc/codex/skills`;
  - explicit invocation as `$name`;
  - optional metadata in `agents/openai.yaml`.

  Whether a repository's `.agents/skills/` is read is **NOT FOUND** in any
  source read.
- **Cursor skills** (<https://cursor.com/docs/skills>): **unverified**, host
  not reachable. Assumed from search results quoting the page:
  - `.cursor/skills/` and `~/.cursor/skills/`, plus `.agents/skills/`,
    `.claude/skills/` and `.codex/skills/` for compatibility;
  - a `/` invocation by name;
  - `disable-model-invocation: true` limiting a skill to explicit
    invocation.
- **GitHub Copilot skills**
  (<https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/ide/copilot-agent-skills>,
  <https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/use-copilot-agents/cloud-agent/create-skills>):
  **unverified**, hosts not reachable. Assumed from search results quoting
  the pages: `.github/skills/`, `.claude/skills/` and `.agents/skills/` in a
  repository, and `~/.copilot/skills/`, `~/.claude/skills/` and
  `~/.agents/skills/` for a user.

# Requirements

## Introduction

The skill render turns one source tree under skills/ into the three af-* skills for each of four coding agents. It reads a skill as a SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter and a body, resolves the reference files the skill links, keeps only the frontmatter keys the agent reads, replaces the one {{invoke}} token with that agent's invocation syntax, and refuses a skill whose body would load more than 24,576 bytes at once. make skills writes the output under build/skills/, make install-skills copies it into an agent's skill directory, and make check runs the render's checks with no network and no credential.

## Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| <source path>: <problem> | The one line the skill render writes to stderr for each problem it finds: the path of the source file, a colon and a space, then the problem in words. Every refusal of the render takes this form, and a warning takes it too. |
| agent | One of the four coding agents the render targets: claude, codex, cursor and copilot. Each reads its own frontmatter keys and its own invocation syntax. |
| body | The part of a SKILL.md that follows the line closing its YAML frontmatter. It is loaded with the skill, which is why it carries the ceiling. |
| reference file | A Markdown file under a skill's own references/ or under skills/_shared/references/, read by the agent at the step that links it rather than loaded with the skill. |
| skill | A directory directly under skills/ whose name does not begin with an underscore, holding a SKILL.md and optionally its own references/ directory. |
| skill render | The program make runs to render, install and uninstall the skills. |

## Requirements

### 14-REQ-1: The skill source tree

**Rationale:** One source tree serves four agents only if the render agrees with the author on what a skill is and on which files belong to it.

#### Criteria

1. [14-REQ-1.1] THE skill render SHALL treat every directory directly under skills/ whose name does not begin with an underscore as a skill, and read its SKILL.md as YAML frontmatter delimited by two --- lines followed by the body
1. [14-REQ-1.2] WHEN a SKILL.md or an included reference file links references/<file>.md, THE skill render SHALL resolve <file>.md in the linking skill's own skills/<name>/references/ first and in skills/_shared/references/ second
   → the resolved file is written into that skill's output as references/<file>.md
1. [14-REQ-1.3] THE skill render SHALL for any skill, include a reference file when that skill's SKILL.md links it or when a reference file already included in that skill links it, and include no other file
1. [14-REQ-1.4] IF a link to references/<file>.md resolves in neither the linking skill's own references/ nor skills/_shared/references/, THEN THE skill render SHALL report the problem and render nothing
   → stderr carries one line reading `skills/af-spec/SKILL.md: links references/tasks.md, which is in neither skills/af-spec/references/ nor skills/_shared/references/`; the exit code is non-zero
1. [14-REQ-1.5] IF a reference file name is present both in a skill's own references/ and in skills/_shared/references/, THEN THE skill render SHALL report the problem naming the file and both directories, and render nothing
   → stderr carries one line of the form `<source path>: <problem>` naming the file and both directories; the exit code is non-zero; no file is written for any agent
1. [14-REQ-1.6] IF a skill directory holds no SKILL.md, or its SKILL.md has no frontmatter, or its frontmatter is not YAML, THEN THE skill render SHALL report which of the three it is and render nothing
   → stderr carries one line of the form `<source path>: <problem>` naming which of the three it is; the exit code is non-zero; no file is written for any agent

### 14-REQ-2: Rendering a skill for an agent

**Rationale:** An installed skill has to work in its agent with no edit, and a render nobody can rerun with the same result is a render nobody can check.

#### Criteria

1. [14-REQ-2.1] WHEN make skills runs over a source tree that holds no problem, THE skill render SHALL write build/skills/<agent>/<name>/SKILL.md and its references/ directory for each of the agents claude, codex, cursor and copilot and each skill under skills/
   → exit code 0; build/skills/<agent>/<name>/SKILL.md exists for all four agents and every skill, each with a references/ holding exactly that skill's included files
1. [14-REQ-2.2] THE skill render SHALL keep in a rendered frontmatter only the keys the agent reads — name, description, argument-hint and disable-model-invocation for claude; name and description for codex; name, description and disable-model-invocation for cursor; name and description for copilot — in the order the source gives them, each kept key carrying its source text and its continuation lines unchanged
1. [14-REQ-2.3] THE skill render SHALL replace every {{invoke <name>}} in a body or a reference file with /<name> for claude, cursor and copilot and with $<name> for codex, and change no other byte of the body or of any reference file
1. [14-REQ-2.4] THE skill render SHALL for any source tree that has not changed, write byte-identical output on every run
1. [14-REQ-2.5] WHEN make skills runs over a source tree from which a file has been removed since the previous run, THE skill render SHALL replace the previous output of make skills whole
   → build/skills/ holds no file that the current source does not render; exit code 0
1. [14-REQ-2.6] THE skill render SHALL render without making a model call, without making a network call, without reading a credential and without running the update-agentkit target

### 14-REQ-3: A skill's name and description

**Rationale:** Every one of the four agents loads a skill by its directory and offers it by its description, so a name or a description that breaks the Agent Skills rule breaks the skill in the agent, not in the render.

#### Criteria

1. [14-REQ-3.1] IF a frontmatter has no name, a name that differs from its directory's name, or a name that is not 1 to 64 characters of lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens with neither the first nor the last character a hyphen, THEN THE skill render SHALL report the rule broken and render nothing
   → stderr carries one line of the form `<source path>: <problem>` naming the rule broken; the exit code is non-zero; no file is written for any agent
1. [14-REQ-3.2] IF a frontmatter has no description, an empty description, or a description longer than 1,024 characters, THEN THE skill render SHALL report which of the three it is and render nothing
   → stderr carries one line of the form `<source path>: <problem>`; a description of exactly 1,024 characters is accepted; the exit code is non-zero; no file is written for any agent

### 14-REQ-4: The body ceiling

**Rationale:** The body is what loads with the skill at every step of a run, so it is the only part whose size the render has to hold down.

#### Criteria

1. [14-REQ-4.1] IF a rendered body is longer than 24,576 bytes for any agent, THEN THE skill render SHALL report the skill, the agent, the size and the overage, and render nothing
   → stderr carries one line reading `skills/af-spec/SKILL.md: body is 31,204 bytes for codex, 6,628 over the 24,576-byte limit`; the exit code is non-zero; no file is written for any agent
1. [14-REQ-4.2] THE skill render SHALL measure a rendered body as the bytes of UTF-8 that follow the line closing the frontmatter, after {{invoke <name>}} has been replaced for that agent, and accept a body of exactly 24,576 bytes
1. [14-REQ-4.3] THE skill render SHALL render a reference file of any size without reporting a problem about its size

### 14-REQ-5: Tokens and agent-specific text

**Rationale:** The one text that differs by agent is the invocation of another skill; any other agent-specific text in the source is a skill that works in one agent and not the next.

#### Criteria

1. [14-REQ-5.1] IF a {{invoke <name>}} token names no directory under skills/, THEN THE skill render SHALL report the source file and the unknown name, and render nothing
   → stderr carries one line of the form `<source path>: <problem>` naming the unknown skill; the exit code is non-zero; no file is written for any agent
1. [14-REQ-5.2] IF a body or a reference file holds a {{...}} token that is not {{invoke <name>}}, THEN THE skill render SHALL report the source file and the token, and render nothing
   → stderr carries one line of the form `<source path>: <problem>` naming the token; the exit code is non-zero; no file is written for any agent
1. [14-REQ-5.3] IF a body or a reference file holds $ARGUMENTS, or holds /<name> or $<name> for a skill under skills/ where the character before it is the start of a line, whitespace or one of a backtick, an opening parenthesis, an opening bracket or a double quote and the character after it is the end of a line, whitespace or punctuation, THEN THE skill render SHALL report the source file and the text found, and render nothing
   → stderr carries one line of the form `<source path>: <problem>` naming the text found and {{invoke <name>}} as its replacement; the exit code is non-zero; the path skills/af-impl written in prose is not reported

### 14-REQ-6: Reporting problems and warnings

**Rationale:** An author fixing the source wants every problem of one run, not the first of five; and a reference file nobody links is worth a word but not a stopped build.

#### Criteria

1. [14-REQ-6.1] THE skill render SHALL report every problem the source tree holds in one run, one problem to a line on stderr in the form `<source path>: <problem>`
1. [14-REQ-6.2] WHEN the source tree holds at least one problem, THE skill render SHALL exit non-zero and write no file for any agent
   → the exit code is non-zero; build/skills/ is left exactly as it was before the run
1. [14-REQ-6.3] WHEN a file in a skill's own references/ is linked by nothing, THE skill render SHALL write a warning to stderr naming the file and leave the exit code 0
   → stderr carries one line reading `skills/af-impl/references/old.md: linked by nothing; not rendered`; the exit code is 0; the file is in no agent's output
1. [14-REQ-6.4] WHEN a file in skills/_shared/references/ is linked by no skill, THE skill render SHALL write a warning to stderr naming the file and leave the exit code 0
   → stderr carries one line naming the file as linked by nothing; the exit code is 0; the file is in no agent's output

### 14-REQ-7: Installing a rendered skill

**Rationale:** A skill reaches an agent only from that agent's own directory, and a user installing again after a source file was removed should not be left with it.

#### Criteria

1. [14-REQ-7.1] WHEN make install-skills runs with no AGENT, THE skill render SHALL render the skills for claude and copy each one into the claude user skill directory
   → exit code 0; ~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md and ~/.claude/skills/<name>/references/ exist for each skill
1. [14-REQ-7.2] THE skill render SHALL resolve the install directory as SKILLS_DIR when SKILLS_DIR is given; else, when PROJECT is given, as <PROJECT>/.claude/skills for claude, <PROJECT>/.agents/skills for codex, <PROJECT>/.cursor/skills for cursor and <PROJECT>/.github/skills for copilot; else as ~/.claude/skills for claude, $CODEX_HOME/skills for codex or ~/.codex/skills when CODEX_HOME is unset, ~/.cursor/skills for cursor and ~/.copilot/skills for copilot
1. [14-REQ-7.3] WHEN the skills are installed, THE skill render SHALL print one line reading `installed: <name> -> <dir>/<name>` for each skill and exit 0
   → stdout carries one such line per skill; the exit code is 0
1. [14-REQ-7.4] THE skill render SHALL replace <dir>/<name>/ whole for each skill installed, leaving behind no file of a previous install, and add, change or remove no other entry under <dir>
1. [14-REQ-7.5] IF the source tree holds at least one problem when an install is asked for, THEN THE skill render SHALL install nothing, report the problems as make skills does, and exit non-zero
   → the exit code is non-zero; stderr carries one line per problem; <dir> is left exactly as it was
1. [14-REQ-7.6] IF AGENT is a value other than claude, codex, cursor or copilot, THEN THE skill render SHALL report the value with the four it accepts and write nothing
   → stderr carries `unknown agent "<value>"; one of: claude, codex, cursor, copilot`; the exit code is non-zero; <dir> is left exactly as it was
1. [14-REQ-7.7] IF PROJECT is given and is not an existing directory, THEN THE skill render SHALL report the path and write nothing
   → stderr carries `PROJECT <path> is not a directory`; the exit code is non-zero; no file is written anywhere
1. [14-REQ-7.8] WHEN the agent also loads another directory that already holds a skill of the name being installed, THE skill render SHALL print the warning naming that directory and install all the same
   → stderr carries `warning: <agent> also loads <path>/<name>; it will see <name> twice`; the exit code is 0; <dir>/<name> holds the installed skill

### 14-REQ-8: Uninstalling the skills

**Rationale:** An uninstall that resolved its directory differently from the install, or that removed more than it installed, would take someone else's skills with it.

#### Criteria

1. [14-REQ-8.1] WHEN make uninstall-skills runs, THE skill render SHALL resolve the directory by the same rule as the install and remove <dir>/<name> for each of af-prd, af-spec and af-impl, printing `removed: <name>` for each one it removed
   → exit code 0; stdout carries one line per removed skill; <dir>/<name> no longer exists for each of the three
1. [14-REQ-8.2] THE skill render SHALL skip a skill name that <dir> does not hold, writing no line for it and leaving the exit code 0
1. [14-REQ-8.3] THE skill render SHALL remove no entry under <dir> other than the directories named af-prd, af-spec and af-impl

### 14-REQ-9: The committed source tree

**Rationale:** The render's rules are worth nothing if the repository's own three skills break them; this is the one criterion the split has to satisfy.

#### Criteria

1. [14-REQ-9.1] THE skill render SHALL render every skill of the repository's own skills/ tree for claude, codex, cursor and copilot without reporting a problem
   → exit code 0 and no line on stderr of the form `<source path>: <problem>`

### 14-REQ-10: The build's targets

**Rationale:** The ceiling and the link rules hold only if the check someone runs before committing is the one that enforces them.

#### Criteria

1. [14-REQ-10.1] WHEN make check runs, THE build SHALL run the render's checks after test, making no network call and reading no API key
   → the exit code is 0 when the source tree holds no problem and non-zero when it holds one, with the problems on stderr; no request leaves the machine
1. [14-REQ-10.2] THE build SHALL list skills, skills-check, install-skills and uninstall-skills in the output of make help
1. [14-REQ-10.3] WHEN make clean runs, THE build SHALL remove build/skills with the rest of build/
   → build/ does not exist; the exit code is 0

## Execution Paths

### 14-PATH-1: A maintainer renders every skill for every agent

1. **maintainer** runs make skills in a checkout
2. **skill render** reads every skill directory under skills/ and resolves the reference files each one links, its own first and the shared ones second
3. **skill render** checks every skill against the render rules for claude, codex, cursor and copilot
4. **skill render** writes build/skills/<agent>/<name>/SKILL.md and its references/ for each agent and skill, replacing any previous output whole
5. **maintainer** reads build/skills/codex/af-spec/SKILL.md and finds only name and description in its frontmatter and $af-impl where the source held {{invoke af-impl}}

### 14-PATH-2: A maintainer installs the skills into a repository and removes them again

1. **maintainer** runs make install-skills AGENT=codex PROJECT=<path> against a scratch repository
2. **skill render** resolves the install directory as <path>/.agents/skills and renders the skills for codex
3. **skill render** replaces <path>/.agents/skills/<name>/ whole for each skill and prints installed: <name> -> <path>/.agents/skills/<name>
4. **maintainer** runs make uninstall-skills AGENT=codex PROJECT=<path>
5. **skill render** removes the three skill directories, prints removed: <name> for each, and leaves every other entry under <path>/.agents/skills in place

### 14-PATH-3: A maintainer sees the render's checks refuse a skill that breaks a rule

1. **maintainer** adds a link to a reference file that does not exist and a body over the ceiling, then runs make skills-check
2. **skill render** collects every problem the source tree holds rather than stopping at the first
3. **skill render** writes one line per problem to stderr, each naming the source file and the rule, and exits non-zero without writing an output tree
4. **maintainer** reads the two problems named, finds build/skills/ unchanged, and sees make check fail on the same checks because it runs skills-check after test

# Test Specification

## Tests

### TS-14-1 (unit): A source tree yields one skill per directory, and underscore directories are not skills

**Verifies:** 14-REQ-1.1

**Given:**

- a source tree with skills/af-prd/SKILL.md, skills/af-spec/SKILL.md, skills/_shared/references/x.md and a loose file skills/notes.md

**When:** the source tree is read

**Then:**

- the skills found are af-prd and af-spec, in that order
- _shared is not among them
- the loose file skills/notes.md is not a skill
- each skill carries its frontmatter text and its body separately, split at the second --- line

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/skillgen/source_test.go, over a fstest.MapFS: skills, problems = readSource(fsys); assert names(skills) == ['af-prd','af-spec']; assert problems is empty; assert skills[0].body starts after the closing ---
```

### TS-14-2 (unit): A skill includes the files it links and the files those link, its own before the shared ones

**Verifies:** 14-REQ-1.2, 14-REQ-1.3

**Given:**

- skills/af-spec/SKILL.md linking references/tasks.md and references/speca-specr.md
- skills/af-spec/references/tasks.md, which itself links references/verdict.md
- skills/af-spec/references/verdict.md
- skills/_shared/references/speca-specr.md
- skills/_shared/references/prd-shape.md, which no skill links

**When:** the files included in af-spec are resolved

**Then:**

- the included set is tasks.md, speca-specr.md and verdict.md
- speca-specr.md resolves to the shared copy because af-spec has none of that name
- prd-shape.md is not included
- a name present in the skill's own references/ resolves there and not in the shared directory

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/skillgen/source_test.go: included = resolveRefs(skills['af-spec']); assert keys(included) == {'tasks.md','speca-specr.md','verdict.md'}; assert included['speca-specr.md'].from == 'skills/_shared/references/speca-specr.md'
```

### TS-14-3 (unit): A link that resolves in neither references directory is a problem naming both directories

**Verifies:** 14-REQ-1.4

**Given:**

- skills/af-spec/SKILL.md linking references/tasks.md, with no tasks.md in either references directory

**When:** the source tree is checked

**Then:**

- one problem is reported
- its text is exactly `skills/af-spec/SKILL.md: links references/tasks.md, which is in neither skills/af-spec/references/ nor skills/_shared/references/`
- no output is produced

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/skillgen/source_test.go: problems = check(fsys); assert problems == [that exact line]
```

### TS-14-4 (unit): One reference file name in both the skill's own and the shared directory is a problem, not an override

**Verifies:** 14-REQ-1.5

**Given:**

- skills/af-spec/references/speca-specr.md and skills/_shared/references/speca-specr.md, both present

**When:** the source tree is checked

**Then:**

- one problem is reported
- it names speca-specr.md and both directories
- no output is produced for any agent

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/skillgen/source_test.go: problems = check(fsys); assert one problem mentioning 'speca-specr.md', 'skills/af-spec/references/' and 'skills/_shared/references/'
```

### TS-14-5 (unit): A skill with no SKILL.md, no frontmatter or frontmatter that is not YAML is a problem naming which

**Verifies:** 14-REQ-1.6

**Given:**

- three source trees: skills/af-x/ with only references/a.md; skills/af-x/SKILL.md starting with # af-x; skills/af-x/SKILL.md whose frontmatter body is `name: [unclosed`

**When:** each tree is checked in turn

**Then:**

- each yields exactly one problem
- the first names skills/af-x as holding no SKILL.md
- the second names skills/af-x/SKILL.md as having no frontmatter
- the third names skills/af-x/SKILL.md and that its frontmatter is not YAML

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/skillgen/source_test.go, a table over the three trees: for each, problems = check(fsys); assert len(problems) == 1 and problems[0] matches the expected `<path>: <problem>`
```

### TS-14-6 (unit): A name is refused when it is missing, differs from its directory or breaks the Agent Skills rule

**Verifies:** 14-REQ-3.1

**Given:**

- a valid skill directory skills/af-spec whose frontmatter name is varied

**When:** the name is absent; is af-impl; is Af-Spec; is af--spec; is -af-spec; is af-spec-; is 65 characters; is a single character a; is 64 characters

**Then:**

- the first seven are each one problem naming the rule broken
- the single character a and the 64-character name are accepted when the directory carries the same name
- no output is produced for any agent when a name is refused

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/skillgen/render_test.go, a table of name -> wantProblem: problems = check(treeWithName(name)); assert (len(problems) > 0) == wantProblem
```

### TS-14-7 (unit): A description is refused when it is missing, empty or over 1,024 characters

**Verifies:** 14-REQ-3.2

**Given:**

- a valid skill directory whose frontmatter description is varied

**When:** the description is absent; is the empty string; is 1,024 characters; is 1,025 characters

**Then:**

- the absent and empty descriptions are each one problem
- 1,024 characters is accepted
- 1,025 characters is one problem naming the limit
- no output is produced for any agent when a description is refused

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/skillgen/render_test.go, a table of description length -> wantProblem
```

### TS-14-8 (unit): A rendered frontmatter keeps only the agent's keys, in the source's order and with its own text

**Verifies:** 14-REQ-2.2

**Given:**

- a SKILL.md whose frontmatter is, in this order, name, description over two lines, argument-hint, disable-model-invocation and metadata with two nested keys

**When:** the skill is rendered for claude, codex, cursor and copilot in turn

**Then:**

- claude keeps name, description, argument-hint and disable-model-invocation and drops metadata
- codex keeps name and description only
- cursor keeps name, description and disable-model-invocation and drops argument-hint
- copilot keeps name and description only
- every kept key appears in the source's order, with its source text and its continuation lines byte for byte

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/skillgen/render_test.go, a table over the four agents: out = render(skill, agent); assert frontmatterKeys(out) == want; assert the description's second line is present unchanged
```

### TS-14-9 (unit): The invoke token becomes the agent's syntax and no other byte of the body or a reference file changes

**Verifies:** 14-REQ-2.3

**Given:**

- a body holding {{invoke af-impl}} twice and a reference file holding {{invoke af-prd}} once, both with surrounding prose, a code block and a table

**When:** the skill is rendered for claude, codex, cursor and copilot in turn

**Then:**

- claude, cursor and copilot carry /af-impl and /af-prd
- codex carries $af-impl and $af-prd
- both occurrences in the body are replaced
- the rendered body and reference file are byte-identical to the source apart from the replaced tokens

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/skillgen/render_test.go, a table over the four agents: out = render(skill, agent); assert out.body == strings.ReplaceAll(source.body, '{{invoke af-impl}}', want)
```

### TS-14-10 (unit): An invoke token naming no skill, and any other brace token, are problems

**Verifies:** 14-REQ-5.1, 14-REQ-5.2

**Given:**

- a source tree whose only skills are af-prd, af-spec and af-impl

**When:** a body holds {{invoke af-fix}}; a body holds {{ARGUMENTS}}; a reference file holds {{invoke}} with no name

**Then:**

- each case yields one problem naming the source file and the token
- the problem for {{invoke af-fix}} names af-fix as a skill that does not exist
- no output is produced for any agent

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/skillgen/render_test.go, a table of token -> expected problem text
```

### TS-14-11 (unit): An argument placeholder or a skill named in an agent's own syntax is a problem, while a path in prose is not

**Verifies:** 14-REQ-5.3

**Given:**

- a source tree whose skills are af-prd, af-spec and af-impl

**When:** a body holds $ARGUMENTS; a body holds `/af-impl <NN>` in a code block; a body holds $af-impl after a space; a body holds the path skills/af-impl/references/landing.md in prose; a reference file holds the word spec/af-impl

**Then:**

- $ARGUMENTS, /af-impl and $af-impl are each one problem naming the text found and {{invoke af-impl}} as its replacement
- the path skills/af-impl/references/landing.md is no problem
- spec/af-impl is no problem
- no output is produced for any agent when a problem is reported

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/skillgen/render_test.go, a table of body text -> wantProblem, covering the delimiters backtick, open paren, open bracket, double quote, line start and whitespace on the left and whitespace, line end and punctuation on the right
```

### TS-14-12 (unit): The body ceiling is measured in bytes after the frontmatter and after substitution, and reference files are not measured

**Verifies:** 14-REQ-4.1, 14-REQ-4.2, 14-REQ-4.3

**Given:**

- a skill whose frontmatter is 300 bytes and whose body length is set per case, and a reference file of 60,000 bytes

**When:** the body is 24,576 bytes; is 24,577 bytes; is 24,576 bytes only because a multi-byte character is counted as one character rather than its bytes; is 24,570 bytes in the source but grows past the ceiling when {{invoke af-impl}} becomes $af-impl for codex

**Then:**

- 24,576 bytes is accepted for all four agents
- 24,577 bytes is one problem reading `skills/af-x/SKILL.md: body is 24,577 bytes for claude, 1 over the 24,576-byte limit`
- the multi-byte case is refused, because the measure is bytes of UTF-8 and not characters
- the case that grows past the ceiling only after substitution is refused for the agent whose substitution is longer, and the frontmatter's 300 bytes are counted in no case
- the 60,000-byte reference file is rendered with no problem about its size

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/skillgen/render_test.go, a table of body -> per-agent want: problems = check(tree); assert the exact overage line for the failing agent
```

### TS-14-13 (unit): Every problem of a run is reported, one to a line, and nothing is written for any agent

**Verifies:** 14-REQ-6.1, 14-REQ-6.2

**Given:**

- a source tree with four problems at once: a broken link in af-prd, a name that differs from its directory in af-spec, an unknown invoke token in af-impl and a body over the ceiling in af-impl
- an output directory already holding a file from a previous run

**When:** the render is asked to write the output tree

**Then:**

- all four problems are on stderr, each on its own line in the form `<source path>: <problem>`
- the exit code is non-zero
- the output directory still holds exactly the file from the previous run and nothing new
- no agent's directory was created

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/skillgen/check_test.go: code, stderr = run(['--out', tmp]); assert code != 0; assert 4 lines, each matching '^[^:]+: '; assert the listing of tmp is unchanged
```

### TS-14-14 (unit): A reference file nothing links is a warning that leaves the exit code 0

**Verifies:** 14-REQ-6.3, 14-REQ-6.4

**Given:**

- skills/af-impl/references/old.md, which no file links
- skills/_shared/references/unused.md, which no skill links
- an otherwise clean source tree

**When:** the render runs

**Then:**

- stderr carries `skills/af-impl/references/old.md: linked by nothing; not rendered`
- stderr carries a line naming skills/_shared/references/unused.md as linked by nothing
- the exit code is 0
- neither file is in any agent's output

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/skillgen/check_test.go: code, stderr = run(['--out', tmp]); assert code == 0; assert both warning lines; assert neither file under tmp
```

### TS-14-15 (integration): The render writes a tree per agent, writes the same bytes on a rerun, and leaves nothing stale behind

**Verifies:** 14-REQ-2.1, 14-REQ-2.4, 14-REQ-2.5

**Given:**

- a clean source tree of three skills with their own and shared reference files
- an empty output directory

**When:** the render runs, then runs again unchanged, then runs again after a reference file and a whole skill have been removed from the source

**Then:**

- the first run writes <out>/<agent>/<name>/SKILL.md and <out>/<agent>/<name>/references/ for all four agents and every skill, and exits 0
- each references/ holds exactly that skill's included files and no other
- the second run writes bytes identical to the first, file for file
- after the third run the removed reference file and the removed skill's directory are gone from every agent's output

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/skillgen/render_test.go, against a real temporary directory: run(['--out', tmp]); snap1 = hashTree(tmp); run again; assert hashTree(tmp) == snap1; remove sources; run again; assert the removed paths are absent for all four agents
```

### TS-14-16 (unit): The render succeeds with no credential in the environment and no reachable network

**Verifies:** 14-REQ-2.6

**Given:**

- a clean source tree
- an environment with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and every other API key unset, and HTTP_PROXY and HTTPS_PROXY pointing at a closed local port

**When:** the render runs

**Then:**

- the exit code is 0
- the output tree is complete for all four agents
- no error about a credential or a connection is reported

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/skillgen/render_test.go: t.Setenv('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY',''), t.Setenv('HTTPS_PROXY','http://127.0.0.1:1'); code = run(['--out', tmp]); assert code == 0
```

### TS-14-17 (unit): The install directory is resolved per agent, with PROJECT and SKILLS_DIR taking precedence in that order

**Verifies:** 14-REQ-7.2

**Given:**

- HOME set to a temporary directory
- CODEX_HOME set in one case and unset in another

**When:** each of the four agents is resolved with no PROJECT and no SKILLS_DIR; with PROJECT set; with SKILLS_DIR set; and with both PROJECT and SKILLS_DIR set

**Then:**

- with neither, the directories are ~/.claude/skills, $CODEX_HOME/skills, ~/.cursor/skills and ~/.copilot/skills, and ~/.codex/skills for codex when CODEX_HOME is unset
- with PROJECT, they are <PROJECT>/.claude/skills, <PROJECT>/.agents/skills, <PROJECT>/.cursor/skills and <PROJECT>/.github/skills
- with SKILLS_DIR, it is SKILLS_DIR for every agent
- with both, SKILLS_DIR wins

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/skillgen/install_test.go, a table of (agent, project, skillsDir, codexHome) -> want: got, err = installDir(...); assert got == want
```

### TS-14-18 (integration): An install copies each skill, names where it put it, replaces the directory whole and leaves its neighbours alone

**Verifies:** 14-REQ-7.1, 14-REQ-7.3, 14-REQ-7.4

**Given:**

- a clean source tree of three skills
- an install directory already holding af-spec/SKILL.md, af-spec/references/stale.md and an unrelated other-skill/SKILL.md

**When:** the install runs for claude with no AGENT given, then runs again after a reference file has been removed from the source

**Then:**

- stdout carries one line per skill reading `installed: <name> -> <dir>/<name>`
- af-spec/references/stale.md is gone after the first install
- other-skill/SKILL.md is untouched after both installs
- the reference file removed from the source is gone from <dir>/<name>/references/ after the second install

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/skillgen/install_test.go, against a real temporary HOME: code, stdout = run(['--install','--skills-dir',dir]); assert code == 0; assert the installed: lines; assert stale.md absent and other-skill intact
```

**Verifies:** 14-REQ-9.1

### TS-14-24 (integration): The build lists the render's targets, runs its checks inside check, and cleans its output

**Verifies:** 14-REQ-10.1, 14-REQ-10.2, 14-REQ-10.3

**When:** make help is run, and the plans of make check and make clean are read with make -n

- the plan of make check runs the render's checks after the test step

- the plan of make clean removes the directory that holds build/skills

in internal/skillgen/make_test.go: out = exec('make','help'); assert the four targets; plan = exec('make','-n','check'); assert skills-check appears after the go test line; plan = exec('make','-n','clean'); assert it removes build. make check is read with -n and never run from a test, because running it would re-enter go test.
```

```


# Tasks

## Test Commands

- **all_tests:** `make test`
- **linter:** `make lint`
- **spec_tests:** `go test ./internal/skillgen/... -count=1`

## Dependencies

None: this spec depends on no other spec.

## Tasks

### [x] 1. Read the skill source tree and resolve the files each skill links (implement, done)

**Criteria:** 14-REQ-1

**Tests:** TS-14-1, TS-14-2, TS-14-3, TS-14-4, TS-14-5

**Steps:**

- 1.1 Create internal/skillgen as package main, with source_test.go holding the behaviours of this task over testing/fstest.MapFS trees, and confirm they fail
- 1.2 In source.go, read a source directory with io/fs: every directory directly under it whose name does not begin with an underscore is a skill, and skills/_shared/references/ is the shared pool
- 1.3 Split each SKILL.md into the raw frontmatter text between the two --- lines and the body that follows the closing line, keeping both as bytes so later steps can filter the frontmatter without re-marshalling it
- 1.4 Collect the Markdown links in a body or a reference file whose target is references/<file>.md, and resolve each one in the skill's own references/ first and in the shared pool second
- 1.5 Walk the links transitively from SKILL.md through the reference files already included, so that a file is included when the skill links it or an included file links it, and no other file is
- 1.6 Report a link that resolves in neither directory with the message the criterion gives, naming the source file, the target and both directories
- 1.7 Report a name present in both the skill's own references/ and the shared pool, and a skill directory with no SKILL.md, no frontmatter, or frontmatter that go-yaml refuses, each as one `<source path>: <problem>` line

**Touches:**

- `internal/skillgen/source.go`
- `internal/skillgen/source_test.go`

**Done when:**

- the tests listed above exist, are executable and pass
- `make test` passes
- `make lint` passes
